name: Major Construction/Minor Maintenance
description: Replacement of major building components (HVAC, roofs, floors, cafeterias) too large for the operating maintenance budget and not listed as a CIP project; funded annually in the Capital Projects Fund, $3.0M one-time in FY27
routing_rule: Smaller facility work not listed as a CIP project; no public dollar cutoff vs the CIP
policy_citation: APS Policy F-5.7 Capital and Maintenance Program and PIP F-5.7 (revisions adopted Aug 13, 2026 under consent; the revised PIP removed the MC/MM committee)

stages.name: Need entered as a work order
stages.venue: School (each facility has a designated coordinator)

stages.name: Facilities assessment and placement in the MC/MM program
stages.venue: Staff; no public list of candidate projects

stages.name: Annual MC/MM funding in the Capital Projects Fund
stages.venue: Budget adoption (Superintendent proposes; Board holds public hearings)

engage.how: A designated coordinator at each school enters work orders; Maintenance Services routes them to a trades division. Ask the front office who that is.
engage.ask: Has this need been entered as a work order, and has Maintenance Services referred it to the MC/MM program or to the CIP?

engage.how: Sign up to speak (2 minutes) when the form opens the week before.
engage.ask: On Aug 13 the CCPTA asked where community engagement occurs in the MC/MM process now that the committee is gone from PIP F-5.7. What is the answer, and where will the MC/MM project list be published?

engage.how: Through your PTA delegate. The CCPTA executive board raised MC/MM transparency with the Board on Aug 13.
engage.ask: Has APS responded to the CCPTA's Aug 13 question on MC/MM engagement? Can the CCPTA ask for the FY27 $3.0M project list?

engage.venue: Advisory Council on School Facilities and Capital Programs
engage.when: Applications through Oct 31, 2026; meets monthly with public minutes
engage.how: Apply through the general advisory council application. The council advises the Board on facilities and the capital program.
engage.ask: How are MC/MM needs identified and prioritized, which projects were deferred this year, and where can a school community see that list?

engage.when: Spring 2027; the Superintendent proposes in late winter and the Board holds hearings before adopting
engage.how: Public hearings are the one scheduled moment the MC/MM allocation is decided in public.
engage.ask: Which projects does the MC/MM allocation fund this year, which were deferred, and by what criteria?

inquiries.question: Where in the MC/MM process does meaningful community engagement occur? If the committee named in the PIP is no longer the vehicle, what will take its place? Will Facilities and Operations publish proposed projects and priorities, and will school communities be able to identify needs and give feedback?
inquiries.why: Asked in public comment by the CCPTA executive board the night the Board adopted revisions to Policy F-5.7 under consent. The revised PIP removed most references to the MC/MM committee. No public answer appears in the Sept 10 or Sept 24 meeting transcripts.

sources.title: Maintenance Services
sources.notes: Work orders entered by a coordinator at each school; MC/MM "funded annually in the Capital Projects Fund"; operating budget covers scheduled maintenance and minor repairs.
